steps.title: Import images and split channels
steps.instruction: Import the confocal z‑stack images into ImageJ (or an equivalent image‑processing program) and split the colour channels into red (dextran‑TMR‑labeled macropinosomes), green (GFP‑expressing cells or GFP‑tagged construct) and blue (DAPI‑stained nuclei).

steps.title: Prepare red channel for segmentation
steps.instruction: Select the red channel, collapse the z‑stack using a Maximum Intensity Projection, convert the resulting image to 8‑bit grayscale, and apply background subtraction with a rolling‑ball algorithm (choose an appropriate rolling‑ball radius based on the signal‑to‑noise ratio of the image).

steps.title: Segment dextran‑positive structures
steps.instruction: Set an appropriate intensity threshold on the processed red image and create a binary image of dextran‑positive structures; optionally apply the watershed filter to separate individual macropinosomes that are closely packed.

steps.title: Mask macropinosomes to GFP‑positive cells (optional)
steps.instruction: If quantitation is to be restricted to GFP‑positive cells, select the green channel, repeat the steps of collapsing, converting to 8‑bit and background subtraction, then threshold to generate a binary GFP mask; use Image Calculator to intersect this mask with the binary macropinosome image from step 3, thereby excluding dextran‑positive structures outside GFP‑positive areas.

steps.title: Analyze macropinosome particles
steps.instruction: Run ImageJ’s Particle Analysis on the segmented macropinosome image with a size filter set to 0.2–20.0 μm² (which corresponds to diameters of 0.5–5.0 μm) to obtain particle counts and measurements of total area, average size, integrated density, and any additional parameters required.

steps.title: Generate nuclei mask
steps.instruction: Select the blue channel of the same confocal z‑stack and repeat steps 2 and 3 (collapse, 8‑bit conversion, background subtraction, thresholding) to produce a binary image of DAPI‑stained nuclei.

steps.title: Count nuclei and compute per‑cell metrics
steps.instruction: Perform Particle Analysis on the nuclei binary image using a size filter that matches the average nucleus area to exclude other DAPI‑positive structures (e.g., mitochondria); save the nuclei count per image and divide the macropinosome measurements obtained in step 5 by this count to calculate average macropinosomes (and other parameters) per cell.
